title: Chinese EV import quota
fact: Canada implemented an initial annual quota of 49,000 EVs originating in China on 1 March 2026.
interp: The quota represents managed market entry and changes the policy context created by the 2024 surtax.
limit: Later allocation rules require continued monitoring.
passage: The quota volume for the first year is 49,000 vehicles. This volume will increase by 6.5% annually.

title: Section 301 strategic tariff modifications
fact: USTR finalized additional or increased Section 301 duties on selected strategic Chinese products in September 2024.
interp: Canada and the United States used different legal authorities despite similar restrictive direction in 2024.
limit: Current combined duty treatment requires tariff-line verification.
passage: The U.S. Trade Representative determined to impose additional Section 301 duties or increase existing duties on certain products of China in strategic sectors.

title: Integrated automotive production
fact: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts were reported as exported to the United States.
interp: U.S. market access and integrated production remain central to Canadian automotive choices.
limit: The source does not provide model-level exposure.
passage: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts are exported to the United States.

title: Agricultural tariff changes
fact: China suspended selected tariffs through the end of 2026 and reduced the combined applied tariff on Canadian canola seed to 14.9%.
interp: The measures partially restored market access after the 2025 deterioration.
limit: The announcement does not establish realized shipment recovery.
passage: Effective March 1, 2026, China suspended specified tariffs and reduced tariffs on Canadian canola seed to a combined applied tariff rate of 14.9%.

title: U.S.–China agriculture comparison boundary
fact: U.S.–China commitments are stored separately and are not treated as applying to Canada.
interp: Parties, products, periods, and legal status must be compared independently.
limit: Current product-level official records remain to be added.
passage: Repository methodology record. No equivalent Canadian commitment is inferred.

title: North American agricultural exposure
fact: No bilateral value is asserted without a definition-compatible official dataset.
interp: Integrated logistics can affect Canadian response options.
limit: Official HS-code trade series should be added before quantification.
passage: Repository gap record pending a comparable official dataset.

title: 2025 bilateral energy trade
fact: In 2025 Canada exported C$157.5 billion and imported C$34.4 billion in specified hydrocarbons with the United States; the U.S. accounted for 90.8% of Canadian hydrocarbon export volume.
interp: Infrastructure and geography give the U.S. relationship structural importance for Canadian energy choices.
limit: The values cover specified hydrocarbons, not all energy.
passage: Exports of crude oil, RPPs, natural gas, and NGLs to the U.S. totaled $157.5 billion for the Canadian economy in 2025.

title: Energy and clean-technology engagement
fact: The 2026 Canada–China roadmap records agreement to support exchanges and cooperation in clean and conventional energy.
interp: The roadmap states a direction for engagement, not a realized project outcome.
limit: Project, financing, offtake and regulatory records are required.
source: Canada–China Economic and Trade Cooperation Roadmap
passage: The roadmap records cooperation and exchanges in energy-related areas.

title: EV battery deployment context
fact: The IEA reported China at 60% of global EV battery deployment in 2025 and the United States at 10%.
interp: The figures illustrate scale relevant to clean-energy competition, not bilateral trade.
limit: Deployment is not capacity, output, exports or ownership.
passage: China represented 60% of global EV battery deployment in 2025 and the United States 10%.

title: Canada–China Financial Working Group
fact: Canada and China launched a Financial Working Group covering financial and monetary policy, markets, stability and regulation, anti-money laundering, cross-border capital flows and global financial governance.
interp: The group establishes dialogue, not commercial market access by itself.
limit: Future implementation outcomes require separate evidence.
passage: The FWG provides a structured and technical channel to enhance bilateral engagement on financial issues.

title: Financial-services market access
fact: The repository does not convert individual firm approvals into a sector-wide market-access conclusion.
interp: Licences, ownership permissions and commercial presence must be recorded separately.
limit: Current regulator-level records remain to be added.
passage: Repository gap record pending regulator-level evidence.

title: Integrated financial relationship
fact: No single bilateral market-access statistic is asserted in this pilot.
interp: Payments, banking, capital markets and prudential coordination require separate evidence domains.
limit: Comparable official records remain to be added.
passage: Repository gap record pending comparable official records.

title: Technology and digital evidence model
fact: The repository separates telecom security, data governance, cyber security, research security, investment screening and connected vehicles.
interp: Separate records prevent different policy instruments from being conflated.
limit: Current instrument-level records remain to be added.
passage: Repository taxonomy record pending instrument-level expansion.

title: Export-control comparison boundary
fact: The repository does not present an exhaustive export-control list from model memory.
interp: A production service should ingest current BIS rules, effective dates, exceptions and superseding notices.
limit: Coverage and licence treatment require current-source review.
source: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
passage: Repository control record requiring current BIS instrument review.

title: Cross-border technology dependency
fact: The repository cross-links connected vehicles, data practices, export controls, investment screening and defence supply chains.
interp: U.S. technology rules can affect Canadian suppliers through integrated market access.
limit: Firm-level effects require transaction evidence.
source: Government of Canada digital policy instruments
passage: Repository cross-link record requiring instrument-level support for consequential claims.

title: Continental and allied security partnerships
fact: DND identifies NORAD, NATO and Five Eyes among Canada’s defence partnerships and describes increased Indo-Pacific engagement.
interp: Continental defence and allied interoperability shape Canadian security choices.
limit: Public sources do not disclose classified operational detail.
passage: Canada maintains defence partnerships including NORAD, NATO and the Five Eyes.

title: Indo-Pacific strategic context
fact: Canada’s Indo-Pacific Strategy provides a long-term framework for engagement in the region, including security and resilience objectives.
interp: Regional strategy should be separated from specific operational measures.
limit: An earlier implementation update is not a complete 2026 status report.
passage: The Indo-Pacific Strategy sets out Canada's regional approach across security, prosperity and resilience.

title: Strategic comparison boundary
fact: The repository does not force symmetry between U.S. and Canadian capabilities, authorities or regional roles.
interp: U.S.–China strategic competition matters to Canada through alliances, supply chains and export controls.
limit: Classified operational evidence is outside this public-source repository.
passage: Repository comparison boundary for public-source research.

title: Border fentanyl seizure context
fact: U.S. northern-border fentanyl seizures were reported as approximately 0.1% of U.S. border-enforcement fentanyl seizures between September 2025 and August 2026.
interp: The figures provide border context but do not measure total trafficking flows.
limit: Seizures should not be equated with production origin or policy effectiveness.
passage: Northern Border seizures accounted for approximately 0.1% of total U.S. fentanyl seizures by U.S. border enforcement between September 2025 and August 2026.

title: Fentanyl precursor supply chain
fact: DEA’s 2025 assessment describes Mexican cartels producing fentanyl using precursor chemicals and pill presses sourced from companies in China.
interp: The evidence describes a multi-country criminal supply chain rather than a direct-China-only flow.
limit: The assessment is not a complete measure of every route.
passage: DEA describes Mexican cartels producing fentanyl using precursor chemicals and pill presses sourced from companies in China.
